mainTopic: Saying הבדלה over a cup and on יום טוב after שבת, and wording in prayer that gets a חזן silenced
overview: This amud finishes the laws of הבדלה and then begins the last משנה of the chapter. רבא rules that even if you said הבדלה in the עמידה, you say it again over a cup of wine, just like קידוש. Next, the גמרא discusses רבי אליעזר's view that הבדלה goes in the ברכה of הודאה. רבי יוחנן's ruling for a יום טוב that falls on מוצאי שבת was reported with different wordings: הלכה, מטין, מודים, and נראין. רב יוסף settles practice with the 'pearl' prayer of רב and שמואל, ותודיענו, which puts הבדלה inside the יום טוב blessing. A new משנה then lists phrases that get a חזן silenced, such as the bird's nest plea and saying מודים twice, and the גמרא explains why. Stories about רבה and רבי חנינא teach that we may not add our own praises of God. A side teaching shows that everything is in Heaven's hands except יראת שמים. The amud ends with רבי זירא's rule about repeating שמע, and רב פפא asks אביי a question whose answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבינא asks רבא for the final ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רבא what the practical הלכה is about saying הבדלה again over a cup after saying it in תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: What is the final ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier part of the גמרא brought opinions that disagree about saying הבדלה over the cup after already saying it in the עמידה. Now רבינא asks רבא which opinion we actually follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to here the גמרא only gave opinions that pull in different directions. רבינא wants a bottom line for practice. This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical ruling (Aramaic for הלכה)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
What is the halakha?
phrases.notes: He is asking which earlier opinion we follow in practice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a ruling on the dispute discussed on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must someone who said הבדלה in the עמידה say it again over a cup of wine?

steps.title: רבא compares הבדלה to קידוש
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that, just like קידוש, הבדלה is said over the cup even if it was already said in תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: It is like קידוש. With קידוש, even though a person already said קידוש in the תפילה, he says קידוש again over the cup. So too with הבדלה: even though he already said הבדלה in the תפילה, he says הבדלה again over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers: yes, you say הבדלה again over the cup. He proves it by comparing it to קידוש, which everyone already does twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that on Friday night we say קידוש in the עמידה and then again over wine at home. רבא says הבדלה works the same way. Saying it in תפילה does not cancel the separate מצוה of saying it over a cup.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctifying שבת or יום טוב at its start
Separating the holy day from the weekday at its end
Prayer, meaning the עמידה (Aramaic for תפילה)

steps.whatToRemember: Final ruling: even if you said הבדלה in the עמידה (אתה חוננתנו), you still make הבדלה over a cup of wine, just as with קידוש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for our practice: we say אתה חוננתנו in מעריב of מוצאי שבת and still make הבדלה over wine.

phrases.english: He said to him: Like kiddush.
Just as with kiddush, even though
one recites kiddush in the prayer,
he still recites kiddush over the cup,
so too havdala as well:
even though one recites havdala in the prayer,
he still recites havdala over the cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבינא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Say הבדלה over the cup even after saying it in תפילה, just like קידוש.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: רבי אליעזר says in הודאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: רבי אליעזר holds that הבדלה is said in the ברכה of הודאה (מודים).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: It is said in the blessing of thanksgiving (מודים).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes רבי אליעזר's opinion from the משנה to start discussing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave several places in the עמידה to insert הבדלה. The תנא קמא says חונן הדעת, and רבי עקיבא says a separate fourth ברכה. רבי אליעזר says the ברכה of הודאה. This line just sets up the story and discussion that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The thanksgiving ברכה of the עמידה (מודים)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two topics. Steps 1 and 2 were about saying הבדלה over a cup. From here on, the topic is where in the עמידה itself הבדלה is inserted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: In the blessing of thanksgiving.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, introducing the next discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the cup and returns to the משנה's next opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, הבדלה is inserted into the ברכה of הודאה.

steps.title: On the road: did רבי יוחנן rule like רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: While רבי זירא rides a donkey, with רבי חייא בר אבין walking behind him, רבי זירא asks him to confirm a report: did he say in רבי יוחנן's name that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר when יום טוב falls right after שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא was riding a donkey, and רבי חייא בר אבין was walking along behind him. He said to him: Is it true that you said in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר when יום טוב falls right after שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to show how רבי אליעזר's opinion is used in practice. רבי זירא asks רבי חייא בר אבין to confirm a ruling he heard in רבי יוחנן's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a יום טוב that starts on מוצאי שבת, the עמידה has no weekday ברכה of חונן הדעת, so the usual place for הבדלה is missing. But the ברכה of הודאה is said every day, including יום טוב. So רבי אליעזר's opinion offers a workable place for הבדלה in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it certain / is it true?

keyTerms.term: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
keyTerms.meaning: A יום טוב that falls right after שבת

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira was riding a donkey,
and walking along
was Rabbi Chiya bar Avin behind him.
He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי זירא asks רבי חייא בר אבין, since רבי חייא בר אבין is the one who said the teaching.

phrases.english: Is it true that you said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan
that the halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת?
phrases.english: on a Festival that falls right after Shabbat?
phrases.notes: No חונן הדעת is said on יום טוב, so the usual place for הבדלה is missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אליעזר's opinion from the משנה to a specific case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי יוחנן really rule like רבי אליעזר for a יום טוב that falls on מוצאי שבת?

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבין confirms: Yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין confirms that רבי יוחנן did rule like רבי אליעזר in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבין answers with one word: yes, the report is true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have a confirmed ruling. On a יום טוב that starts on מוצאי שבת, the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר according to רבי יוחנן. The next step will question what this ruling implies.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי אליעזר for a יום טוב that falls after שבת.

steps.title: Saying 'the הלכה follows him' implies a dispute: who disagrees?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that saying 'the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר' implies that others disagree in this case. It asks who they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The הלכה follows him'? That implies that others disagree with him here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא examines the wording of the ruling. You only need to say 'the הלכה follows X' if someone argues with X. So it asks: who argues in this case? This sets up the next part of the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a יום טוב after שבת, חונן הדעת is not said, so the תנא קמא's usual place is not available. It seems no other option exists, so why would anyone disagree with רבי אליעזר? The גמרא wants to find the opposing view that makes the word 'הלכה' necessary.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to the ruling itself. The גמרא is only asking what the word 'הלכה' implies, namely that some opposing opinion exists in this case.

phrases.english: 'The halakha' implies that they disagree?
phrases.notes: A ruling is only needed where there is a dispute. Where is the dispute?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of the ruling just confirmed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who disagrees with רבי אליעזר about a יום טוב that falls after שבת, given that the word 'הלכה' implies a dispute?
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'הלכה כרבי אליעזר' in רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling formula implies a dispute. But in this case there seems to be no other option, so no one should disagree.

steps.title: The Rabbis seem to disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the רבנן as possible opponents of רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do they not disagree? But the Rabbis disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the difficulty raised in step 6: why look for someone who disagrees when the רבנן already do?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן place הבדלה differently from רבי אליעזר during the year. The challenge assumes their disagreement also applies when יום טוב follows שבת.

phrases.english: And do they not disagree? But the Rabbis disagree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the רבנן as the apparent answer to the question of who disagrees.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that there is no disagreement with רבי אליעזר in this case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר about where הבדלה is said, so they appear to supply the missing disagreement.

steps.title: Their disagreement may apply only on other days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the known disagreement of the רבנן to the rest of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that the Rabbis disagree on the other days of the year. But when a Festival falls immediately after Shabbat, do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the disagreement of the רבנן does not necessarily extend to a יום טוב immediately after שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A disagreement in the usual case does not prove a disagreement in this special case. The רבנן might agree with רבי אליעזר here.

keyTerms.meaning: say, or perhaps we should say
on the other days of the year

keyTerms.term: בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
keyTerms.meaning: when a Festival falls immediately after Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דִּפְלִיגִי רַבָּנַן בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: Say that the Rabbis disagree on the other days of the year,

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת מִי פְּלִיגִי?
phrases.english: but when a Festival falls immediately after Shabbat, do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דִּפְלִיגִי רַבָּנַן בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the disagreement cited in step 7 to cases other than the one under discussion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The רבנן as proven opponents of רבי אליעזר when יום טוב follows שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their disagreement on ordinary days does not establish that they disagree in this special case.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא still disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers רבי עקיבא as a different opponent of רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי עקיבא disagrees!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge: even if the רבנן might agree here, רבי עקיבא disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gives הבדלה its own ברכה. That is different from רבי אליעזר’s placement of הבדלה in הודאה.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Akiva disagrees!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבנן are set aside as a proven disagreement in this case, the גמרא points instead to רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to explain why a ruling like רבי אליעזר needs to be stated.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא explicitly offers a different placement for הבדלה.

steps.title: The established number of blessings rules out רבי עקיבא’s practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא’s separate ברכה is not followed here, just as it is not followed during the rest of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we follow רבי עקיבא throughout the year, such that we should now follow him? Why do we not follow רבי עקיבא throughout the year? Eighteen blessings were instituted, not nineteen. Here too, seven were instituted, not eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא’s view is not followed as the practice in this case. It compares the fixed number of ברכות here with the fixed number during the rest of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving הבדלה a separate ברכה would add to the established count: nineteen instead of eighteen during the year, or eight instead of seven here. So רבי עקיבא's view is not taken into account in this case, and it cannot be the opposing opinion that the word הלכה implies. The question of who disagrees is back, and step 11 deals with it.
steps.whatToRemember: Since his extra ברכה is never followed, רבי עקיבא's view does not count as a real opponent here. The word הלכה still lacks an opponent, which leads to the correction in step 11.

phrases.english: Is it that throughout the entire year

phrases.aramaic: מִי עָבְדִינַן כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּהַשְׁתָּא נֵיקוּ וְנַעֲבֵיד כְּווֹתֵיהּ?!
phrases.english: we follow Rabbi Akiva, such that now we should get up and follow him?!
Throughout the entire year, what is the reason
we do not follow Rabbi Akiva?

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַמְנֵי סְרֵי תַּקּוּן, תְּשַׁסְרֵי לָא תַּקּוּן.
phrases.english: Because eighteen were instituted; nineteen were not instituted.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, שָׁב תַּקּוּן תַּמְנֵי לָא תַּקּוּן.
phrases.english: Here too, seven were instituted; eight were not instituted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ מִי עָבְדִינַן כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why רבי עקיבא’s disagreement does not make his approach the practice for this case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies the established count of ברכות to the proposed extra ברכה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because רבי עקיבא disagrees, his separate ברכה might be followed when יום טוב follows שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The established count is seven ברכות here, not eight, just as it is eighteen rather than nineteen during the year.

steps.title: The ruling was stated more cautiously
steps.stepSummary: The earlier wording is corrected: it said מַטִּין, not הֲלָכָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was not stated as ‘the law follows’; rather, it was stated as ‘one inclines toward this view.’
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers רבי חייא בר אבין's difficulty by correcting the wording that caused it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הֲלָכָה sounded like a firm ruling against an opposing view. מַטִּין expresses a preference without making that same claim.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was not ‘the law follows’ that was stated,
but rather ‘one inclines toward it’ was stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rather than proposing another opponent, this answer revisits the wording behind the original question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement used הֲלָכָה, implying an opposing position.
steps.terutzMaskana: The statement used מַטִּין, which does not require that inference.

steps.title: Two versions of the wording are reported
steps.stepSummary: A report in the name of רַבֵּנוּ is transmitted in two versions: הֲלָכָה and מַטִּין.
steps.simpleTranslation: For it was stated: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said in the name of our teacher, ‘The law follows’; and some say the wording was, ‘One inclines toward it.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a report showing why the precise wording needs attention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same report is preserved with two different words. That supports the previous step’s need to distinguish הֲלָכָה from מַטִּין.

phrases.english: For it was stated: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avdimi
said in the name of our teacher: ‘The law follows,’
and some say: ‘One inclines toward it.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This report supplies the two wordings distinguished in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling was transmitted with differing degrees of certainty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two versions reported by רבי יצחק בר אבדימי in the name of רַבֵּנוּ.

steps.title: Two more ways to describe the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports agreement, while רבי חייא בר אבא reports that the view appears correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said, ‘They agree.’ And רבי חייא בר אבא said, ‘It appears correct.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more reported descriptions of how רבי אליעזר’s view is treated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוֹדִים says the other sages agree with רבי אליעזר here. נִרְאִין says his view appears right, without saying that everyone agrees.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: ‘They agree.’

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: נִרְאִין.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: ‘It appears correct.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two versions in step 12, the גמרא records two further formulations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן says מוֹדִים; רבי חייא בר אבא says נִרְאִין.

steps.title: Rely on the carefully transmitted version
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא recommends retaining רבי חייא בר אבא’s wording because he transmitted teachings carefully.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Keep רבי חייא בר אבא’s version in hand, for he was precise and learned the teaching well from its originator, like רחבא of פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא tells the learner which version to keep and gives a reason to trust its transmission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason concerns how accurately רבי חייא בר אבא learned the teaching from its source. The comparison to רחבא דפומבדיתא reinforces that point about careful transmission.

keyTerms.meaning: from the mouth of its originator
רחבא of פומבדיתא, known for careful transmission

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא does not treat הֲלָכָה, מַטִּין, מוֹדִים, and נִרְאִין as interchangeable. רבי זירא favors the carefully transmitted wording נִרְאִין.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Hold on to
the version of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba,
for he was precise and learned the teaching
well from the mouth of its originator,
like Raḥava of Pumbedita.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: נְקוֹט דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא בִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי זירא selects רבי חייא בר אבא’s wording from the reports just listed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Retain רבי חייא בר אבא’s formulation, נִרְאִין, as the carefully transmitted wording.

steps.title: רחבא keeps his teacher's exact word for the Temple porticoes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows how careful רבי חייא בר אבא's kind of transmission is. רחבא quoted רבי יהודה's unusual word סטיו instead of switching to the common word.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רחבא said in the name of רבי יהודה: The Temple Mount was a double colonnade (סטיו), with one colonnade inside another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an example of a student who repeated his teacher's exact words. This backs up רבי זירא's claim in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The content about the Temple Mount is not the point here. The point is that רחבא said סטיו, the word his teacher used, and not the everyday word אצטבא. This shows what 'careful transmission' looks like, and it is why רבי חייא בר אבא's wording 'נראין' is the one to trust.

keyTerms.meaning: A colonnade or portico (row of columns). It was רבי יהודה's own word.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the architecture of the Temple Mount. The גמרא quotes this line only to show how carefully רחבא kept his teacher's exact word.

phrases.english: As Rachava said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda:
phrases.notes: The 'ד' (as) connects this example to רבי זירא's praise of careful transmitters.

phrases.english: The Temple Mount was a double colonnade,
phrases.notes: He used his teacher's word סטיו instead of the common word אצטבא.

phrases.english: and there was a colonnade within a colonnade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an illustration that supports רבי זירא's description of רבי חייא בר אבא as a careful transmitter.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that careful students keep their teacher's exact wording, so רבי חייא בר אבא's version should be kept.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רחבא quoting רבי יהודה with the unusual word סטיו.

steps.title: רב יוסף relies on the 'pearl' of רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he does not decide based on either reported version. He relies instead on the formula that רב and שמואל instituted in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I don't know this, and I don't know that. But I do know from רב and שמואל that they set up a 'pearl' for us in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף settles the practical question. Instead of choosing among the reported wordings ('הלכה', 'מטין', 'מודים', 'נראין'), he points to an established prayer formula from רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier debate was about how strongly רבי אליעזר's view was endorsed (הלכה, מטין, מודים, or נראין). רב יוסף steps around that whole question. Practice in בבל follows a ready-made formula that puts הבדלה inside the יום טוב blessing. He calls it a 'pearl' because it is so beautifully worded.

keyTerms.meaning: I don't know this (I am not relying on this version).
A pearl. Here it means a precious, beautifully worded prayer text.

steps.whatToRemember: The final practice is not based on 'הלכה' or 'מטין'. It is based on the formula of רב and שמואל, which blends הבדלה into the יום טוב blessing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the 'ותודיענו' paragraph that is said in the עמידה when יום טוב falls on מוצאי שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I do not know this one
phrases.notes: He means one of the two versions (for example, 'הלכה').

phrases.english: and I do not know that one,
phrases.notes: He means the other version (for example, 'מטין').

phrases.english: but from Rav and Shmuel I know,
that they instituted for us a pearl in Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אֲנָא לָא הַאי יָדַעְנָא וְלָא הַאי יָדַעְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the debate about how to report the ruling, and settles practice with an established formula.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When יום טוב falls on מוצאי שבת, הבדלה is included in the middle blessing of the יום טוב עמידה, using רב and שמואל's formula.

steps.title: The wording of the 'pearl' formula
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the full text of רב and שמואל's formula. It praises God for the holy times and also separates שבת from יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: You made known to us, ה׳ our God, Your just laws, and taught us to do the decrees You desire. You gave us times of joy and festivals of free-will offerings. You gave us the holiness of שבת, the honor of the festival, and the festive offering of the רגל. You separated between the holiness of שבת and the holiness of יום טוב, and You made the seventh day holy above the six workdays. You separated and made holy Your people ישראל with Your holiness. And You gave us, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the actual words of the 'pearl' that רב יוסף mentioned. This is the text itself, not a new argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula first praises the holiness of the festivals. Then it adds the הבדלה themes: the separation between שבת and יום טוב, and between the seventh day and the workdays. So one blessing does both jobs. It sanctifies the יום טוב and it makes הבדלה for שבת, with no separate blessing needed. It ends with 'ותתן לנו', where the regular יום טוב text picks up again.

keyTerms.meaning: And You made known to us. This is the opening word of the formula.
The festive offering brought on the pilgrimage festival.
You separated. This is the הבדלה theme.
Etc. It means continue with the usual text.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a separate fourth blessing. It is inserted into the regular middle blessing of יום טוב, and the normal text continues at 'ותתן לנו'.

phrases.english: "You have made known to us, Lord our God, Your righteous laws,
and taught us to perform the decrees of Your will,
and given us as a heritage seasons of joy and festivals of free-will offerings,
and bequeathed to us the holiness of Shabbat,
and the glory of the festival and the festive offering of the pilgrimage festival.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת לִקְדוּשַּׁת יוֹם טוֹב הִבְדַּלְתָּ,
phrases.english: Between the holiness of Shabbat and the holiness of the Festival You have distinguished,
phrases.notes: Here the הבדלה theme begins.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה קִדַּשְׁתָּ.
phrases.english: and the seventh day You made holy over the six days of work.

phrases.aramaic: הִבְדַּלְתָּ וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ אֶת עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְדוּשָּׁתֶךָ.
phrases.english: You distinguished and sanctified Your people Israel with Your holiness.
And You have given us, etc."
phrases.notes: From here the regular יום טוב blessing continues.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַתּוֹדִיעֵנוּ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֶת מִשְׁפְּטֵי צִדְקֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the content of the 'pearl' that רב יוסף referred to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יום טוב middle blessing on מוצאי שבת contains the הבדלה themes inside it, using this exact wording.

steps.title: משנה: prayer phrases that get the leader silenced
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a שליח ציבור who says 'Your mercy reaches the bird's nest', 'May Your name be mentioned for the good', or 'מודים, מודים' is silenced.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who says: 'Your mercy extends to the bird's nest', or 'May Your name be remembered for the good', or 'We thank, we thank', is silenced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes a new משנה. It lists three problematic phrases in prayer, and says the person who says them is stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives no reasons yet. The coming גמרא will explain what is wrong with each phrase. Roughly: the bird's nest phrase misreads God's commands as mercy. 'For the good' implies thanks only for good things. Saying 'מודים' twice suggests two powers. The ruling itself is simple: the community stops him.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird's nest. This refers to the מצוה of sending away the mother bird.
May Your name be mentioned or remembered.

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the final prayer-related section of the chapter. It teaches that the wording of תפילה must not suggest wrong beliefs.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who says: "Your mercy extends to the bird's nest,"
or "May Your name be mentioned for the good,"
or "We give thanks, we give thanks": they silence him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוֹמֵר: ״עַל קַן צִיפּוֹר יַגִּיעוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic after the הבדלה discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח ציבור who says these three phrases is silenced.

steps.title: Two of the three silenced phrases are easy to explain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why 'מודים, מודים' and 'על טוב יזכר שמך' are silenced. This sets up a question about the third phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It makes sense that we silence someone who says 'מודים, מודים', because it looks like he is thanking two separate powers. It also makes sense to silence 'על טוב יזכר שמך'. That phrase suggests praise only for the good and not for the bad. But we learned in a משנה that a person must bless God for the bad just as he blesses Him for the good.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the משנה by explaining the two easy cases. It uses 'בשלמא' ('granted') to set up a question about the case that is still unexplained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'מודים' twice can sound like thanking two gods, which is a serious theological problem. 'על טוב יזכר שמך' limits praise to the good, which goes against a משנה that requires blessing God for the bad as well. The bird's nest case has no obvious reason yet, and the next step asks about it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that comes after the משנה
'Granted' or 'it makes sense'. It introduces the easy cases before asking about a hard one.
They silence him, meaning they stop the חזן
Two powers or authorities, the heretical belief in more than one god

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'בשלמא' is giving the final answer for all three cases. It only explains the first two so the גמרא can then ask about the third.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Granted, 'We give thanks, we give thanks' —
they silence him
because it appears like two authorities.
And 'May Your name be mentioned for the good' also makes sense:

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁמַע עַל הַטּוֹבָה וְלֹא עַל הָרָעָה,
phrases.english: it implies for the good and not for the bad,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה
phrases.english: and we learned: A person is obligated to bless for the bad
just as he blesses for the good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in Step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'מודים, מודים' is silenced because it suggests two powers. 'על טוב יזכר שמך' is silenced because it excludes blessing for the bad.

steps.title: Why is the bird's nest phrase forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is wrong with saying 'Your mercy reaches the bird's nest'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the phrase 'Your mercy reaches the bird's nest' — what is the reason they silence him?
steps.whatsHappening: Having explained the two easy cases, the גמרא now asks about the hard one. It wants to know why it is wrong to praise God's mercy toward the bird's nest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This phrase seems like a nice praise. It points to the מצוה of sending away the mother bird and calls it divine mercy. The גמרא wants to know what problem the משנה saw in it.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird's nest. This refers to the מצוה of שילוח הקן, sending away the mother bird before taking the young.
'But' or 'however'. It turns from the easy cases to the hard one.

phrases.english: But 'Your mercy reaches the bird's nest' —
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא עַל קַן צִפּוֹר יַגִּיעוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא' setup by asking about the case that is still unexplained
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the משנה silences someone who praises God's mercy on the bird's nest

steps.title: Two אמוראים give two reasons
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין and רבי יוסי בר זבידא disagree. One says the phrase creates jealousy among creations. The other says it wrongly turns God's commands into mercy, when they are really decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two אמוראים in ארץ ישראל disagreed about this: רבי יוסי בר אבין and רבי יוסי בר זבידא. One said: because he causes jealousy among the creations. The other said: because he makes the commandments of the הקדוש ברוך הוא into acts of mercy, when they are only decrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with two opinions. Each one names a different problem with the bird's nest phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason 1: singling out birds for mercy makes it sound like God favors them over other creatures, which stirs up 'jealousy' in creation. Reason 2: the מצוות are not explained as God's feelings of mercy. They are royal decrees that we obey whether or not we know the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The works of creation, meaning all created beings
His attributes or ways. Here it means God's commandments.
Decrees, commands given without a stated reason

steps.whyThisMatters: The second reason became a famous principle. Do not present מצוות as being only about God's mercy, because they are the King's decrees.

phrases.english: Two amora'im in the West (Eretz Yisrael) disagreed about it,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר זְבִידָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin and Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida:
One said: because he casts jealousy
among the works of creation.
And one said: because he makes the attributes
of the Holy One, Blessed be He, into mercy,
when they are nothing but decrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the phrase causes jealousy among creations, or it wrongly presents God's decrees as mercy.

steps.title: A חזן uses the bird's nest phrase and רבה praises him
steps.stepSummary: A prayer leader in front of רבה asked for mercy using the bird's nest, and רבה praised his skill in appeasing God.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man went down before the ark in front of רבה and said: 'You had pity on the bird's nest, have pity and mercy on us.' רבה said: How well this young תלמיד חכם knows how to appease his Master!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which someone says the very phrase the משנה forbids. Surprisingly, רבה praises him. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story seems to clash directly with the משנה. רבה appears to approve of a phrase that the משנה says should be silenced, and this creates the tension.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down before the ark, meaning he served as חזן

phrases.english: A certain person who descended (to lead prayer) before Rabba

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר: אַתָּה חַסְתָּ עַל קַן צִפּוֹר,
phrases.english: and said: You had pity on the bird's nest,
You, have pity and mercy on us.
Rabba said: How much does he know,
this young scholar, how to appease his Master!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that seems to go against the משנה's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה seemingly praised a חזן who used the bird's nest phrase

steps.title: אביי objects that the משנה says to silence him
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: our משנה rules that someone who says this is silenced.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But didn't we learn in the משנה that we silence him?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's praise by pointing to the משנה. It says this exact phrase gets the חזן silenced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is direct: a משנה outranks an אמורא's reaction. If the משנה forbids the phrase, how can רבה praise it?

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But we learned that they silence him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's praise in Step 22
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says to silence someone who says the bird's nest phrase, so praising him contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: רבה was only testing אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבה also agreed with the משנה. He praised the חזן only to sharpen אביי's mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה too held like the משנה. He just wanted to sharpen אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem. רבה never disagreed with the משנה. He said it on purpose to see if אביי would catch the mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction disappears: רבה's praise was a teaching test, not a real ruling. The משנה's law stays fully in place: someone who says the bird's nest phrase is silenced.

keyTerms.meaning: To sharpen, meaning to test and train the mind

steps.whatToRemember: There are three phrases a חזן is silenced for. 'מודים, מודים' suggests two powers. 'על טוב יזכר שמך' praises only for the good. The bird's nest phrase either causes jealousy in creation or turns God's decrees into mercy. רבה's praise was only a test for אביי, so the משנה's ruling stands.

phrases.english: And Rabba too (held like the mishna);
he wanted to sharpen Abaye.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה נָמֵי, לְחַדּוֹדֵי אַבָּיֵי הוּא דְּבָעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting intent: the statement was a test, not a ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה truly approved of the bird's nest phrase, against the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה agreed with the משנה and only spoke to sharpen אביי

steps.title: A prayer leader adds many extra praises of God
steps.stepSummary: A חזן leading davening before רבי חנינא lists many more praises of God than the standard three.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man led the prayer in front of רבי חנינא. He said: 'The God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome, and the powerful, and the strong, and the feared, the strong, the mighty, the certain, the honored.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about a חזן who adds a long list of praises in the first ברכה of שמונה עשרה. This sets up רבי חנינא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The standard text has only three praises: הגדול הגבור והנורא. This חזן kept going and added seven more. It continues the theme of the previous steps, which dealt with things a שליח ציבור should not say.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down before him, meaning he led the prayer (the תיבה was placed lower)
The three standard praises in the first ברכה of שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: A certain man who went down (to lead the prayer) before Rabbi Chanina
said: "The God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome,
and the powerful, and the strong, and the feared,
the strong, the mighty, the certain, and the honored."
phrases.notes: Seven praises beyond the standard three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like the story of the חזן before רבה in step 22, this is another story of a שליח ציבור saying something questionable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזן added many praises beyond the standard three.

steps.title: רבי חנינא rebukes the prayer leader
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא waits until the חזן finishes, then tells him that even the three standard praises are only allowed because משה רבינו and אנשי כנסת הגדולה set them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא waited until he finished. When he finished, he said to him: 'Did you finish all the praises of your Master? Why do we need all this? Even the three praises we say, if משה רבינו had not said them in the תורה, and אנשי כנסת הגדולה had not put them into davening, we would not be allowed to say them. And you went on and said all of these!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא criticizes the חזן for adding extra praises. He explains that we may not invent our own praises of God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three praises have two sources of permission: משה רבינו wrote them in the תורה (דברים י:יז), and אנשי כנסת הגדולה fixed them in תפלה. Without both, even those three would be off limits. So adding more praises on your own is not extra honor. It is overstepping.

keyTerms.meaning: The praises of your Master (said with irony)
The Men of the Great Assembly, who set the text of davening

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנינא is not saying the extra words are false. Every one of them is true about God. His point is that any list of praises we make up is limited, so it ends up making God seem smaller, not greater.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that we do not add our own praises of God to the fixed text of תפלה.

phrases.english: He waited for him until he finished.
When he finished, he said to him:
Have you finished all the praises of your Master?!
phrases.notes: Said with irony: God's praises have no end.

phrases.english: Why do I need all this?
We, these three (praises) that we say,

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּאַמְרִינְהוּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ בְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: if Moshe our teacher had not said them in the Torah,
and the Men of the Great Assembly had not come
and established them in the prayer,
we would not be able to say them,
and you said all of these and kept going!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי חנינא responds to the חזן's extra praises.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We may say only the praises set by the תורה and by אנשי כנסת הגדולה, and we may not add more on our own.

steps.title: The parable of the king praised for his silver
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא illustrates his point: praising a king who owns countless gold coins for having silver ones is an insult.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a human king who had a million gold coins, and people praised him for having silver coins. Isn't that an insult to him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives a parable to explain why extra praises are actually disrespectful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any list of praises we can come up with is like 'silver' compared to God's real 'gold,' which has no limit. A long list makes it sound as if we have described God fully, and that makes Him seem small. So the parable shows that adding praises lowers God's honor instead of raising it.

keyTerms.meaning: A human king (literally, of flesh and blood)

steps.whatToRemember: Extra praises of God are not more honor. Because any human praise is limited, piling them up suggests God can be fully described, and that is a kind of insult.

phrases.english: A parable: it is like a king of flesh and blood

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ אֶלֶף אֲלָפִים דִּינְרֵי זָהָב,
phrases.english: who had a thousand thousand gold dinars,
and they were praising him for (owning) silver ones.
Isn't that an insult to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It supports רבי חנינא's rebuke with a parable.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's claim that extra praises are improper
steps.raayaSupportSource: A parable about a human king praised for silver when he owns vast gold

steps.title: Everything is in Heaven's hands except fear of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי חנינא: God decides everything except whether a person will have יראת שמים, as the פסוק shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנינא said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except fear of Heaven. As it says: 'And now, Israel, what does ה׳ your God ask of you, except to fear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching of the same רבי חנינא. It is a side topic about free choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God decides a person's life circumstances, but whether he fears God is his own choice. The proof is that the פסוק says God 'asks' it of us. You only ask for something the other person has the power to give.

keyTerms.meaning: Everything is in the hands of Heaven

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for בחירה חופשית: a person's spiritual choices are truly his own.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina said:
Everything is in the hands of Heaven,
except for fear of Heaven.
As it is said: "And now, Israel,
what does ה׳ your God ask of you
except to fear."
phrases.notes: דברים י:יב

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: הַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It is linked only because the speaker is the same רבי חנינא. It is a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everything is decided by Heaven except a person's יראת שמים, which is his own choice.

steps.title: Is fear of Heaven really a small thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of the פסוק: it makes יראת שמים sound like a small request, yet God's only treasure is יראת שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is fear of Heaven a small thing? But רבי חנינא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: The Holy One has nothing in His treasure house except a treasure of fear of Heaven, as it says: 'Fear of ה׳ is His treasure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on the פסוק just quoted. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'what does God ask of you, except to fear' sounds as if fear of God is a small, easy request. But another teaching says יראת שמים is the most precious thing God has. A treasure that rare and valuable cannot be called small.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so that...? (opens a challenging question)

steps.confusionAlert: This question does not attack רבי חנינא's rule that יראת שמים is in our hands. It attacks the פסוק's tone, 'what does God ask... only fear,' which makes it sound minor.

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם מִילְּתָא זוּטַרְתָּא הִיא?
phrases.english: Is fear of Heaven a small thing?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chanina say in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּבֵית גְּנָזָיו
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, has nothing in His treasure house
except a treasure of fear of Heaven,
as it is said: "Fear of ה׳ is His treasure."
phrases.notes: ישעיה לג:ו

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם מִילְּתָא זוּטַרְתָּא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges how the פסוק cited in step 28 describes יראת שמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the פסוק 'what does ה׳ ask of you except to fear,' which implies fear of God is a small request
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that יראת שמים is God's only treasure, which shows it is extremely precious and not a small request.

steps.title: For משה, יראת שמים really was a small thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that from משה רבינו's point of view, יראת שמים was a small request.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, for משה, it is a small matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 29. It agrees that the פסוק calls יראת שמים a small thing, because משה רבינו is the one saying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא was that יראת שמים is God's greatest treasure, so how can the פסוק treat it as a small request? The answer is that the size of a request depends on who is speaking. משה had so much יראת שמים that, to him, asking for it felt minor.

keyTerms.meaning: In relation to / from the perspective of

phrases.english: Yes, in relation to Moshe
phrases.notes: The גמרא accepts the wording of the פסוק and explains it.

phrases.english: it is a small matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, לְגַבֵּי מֹשֶׁה מִילְּתָא זוּטַרְתָּא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Perspective distinction: the פסוק describes how the request looks from משה's level, not how it looks in absolute terms.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to call יראת שמים small in general, which contradicts its being God's only treasure.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is small only from משה רבינו's point of view, because he already had it in full.

steps.title: Parable of the large and small vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא compares this to a person asked for a vessel. If he owns it, even a big one feels small. If he lacks it, even a small one feels big.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חנינא said: This is like a person who is asked for a large vessel. If he has it, it seems to him like a small vessel. If he is asked for a small one and does not have it, it seems to him like a large vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a parable from רבי חנינא. It shows that something feels small or big depending on whether you already have it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being asked for something you own feels easy, even if the thing is large. Being asked for something you lack feels hard, even if the thing is small. משה owned יראת שמים, so for him it was a 'small vessel.'
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק calls יראת שמים small only because משה רבינו, who said it, already had it fully. Something you own feels small, and something you lack feels big.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם שֶׁמְבַקְּשִׁים מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלִי גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: A parable: to a person from whom they request a large vessel,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ לוֹ — דּוֹמֶה עָלָיו כִּכְלִי קָטָן.
phrases.english: and he has it — it seems to him like a small vessel.
If he is asked for a small one, and he does not have it —
it seems to him like a large vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 30 with a parable.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that יראת שמים could truly be called 'small' from משה's perspective.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's parable of a person asked for a vessel he has or lacks.

steps.title: The משנה: repeating מודים gets you silenced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a חזן who says 'מודים מודים' is silenced.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'We give thanks, we give thanks,' they silence him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה, about saying 'מודים' twice. It is setting up a discussion about whether other repeated words get the same treatment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying מודים twice is serious enough that the person is stopped in the middle. The usual explanation is that it looks like thanking two different powers. This rule becomes the comparison point for רבי זירא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We give thanks', the opening of the thanksgiving ברכה in שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: "We give thanks, we give thanks"
they silence him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the aggadic discussion back to the next clause of the משנה.

steps.title: רבי זירא: repeating שמע is like repeating מודים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rules that someone who says 'שמע שמע' is treated like someone who says 'מודים מודים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Anyone who says 'שמע, שמע' is like one who says 'מודים, מודים.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא extends the משנה's rule. Repeating the words of קריאת שמע is just as bad as repeating מודים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating שמע can also look like accepting two different powers. So רבי זירא puts it in the same category, which seems to mean this person is also silenced. That last point is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Hear', the opening word of קריאת שמע

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Anyone who says "Shema, Shema" —
is like one who says "Modim, Modim."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר ״שְׁמַע שְׁמַע״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's rule about מודים to קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeating 'שמע' is treated the same as repeating 'מודים', so the person is silenced.

steps.title: A ברייתא says repeating שמע is only disgraceful
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא calls repeating שמע 'מגונה' (disgraceful), which implies the person is not silenced. This seems to go against רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection from a ברייתא: One who reads שמע and doubles it, this is disgraceful. Disgraceful, yes, but they do not silence him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא with a ברייתא. The ברייתא uses a milder word, 'disgraceful,' and never says to silence the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא compared repeating שמע to repeating מודים, where the person is silenced. The ברייתא only calls it 'disgraceful.' This implies a lesser level: it is wrong, but nobody stops him. So the two sources seem to disagree.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says 'do not silence him' outright. The גמרא infers it from the milder word 'מגונה.' If silencing were required, the ברייתא would have said so.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who reads Shema and doubles it —
this is disgraceful.
Disgraceful is what it is,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reading this from the way the ברייתא words it.

phrases.english: but silence him we do not!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְכוֹפְלָהּ הֲרֵי זֶה מְגוּנֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's ruling in Step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that repeating שמע is like repeating מודים, where the person is silenced.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא labels repeating שמע only as 'מגונה,' which implies a lesser response with no silencing. That contradicts treating it exactly like מודים.

steps.title: Repeating word by word versus repeating verse by verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The ברייתא, which says repeating is only מגונה, speaks of someone who repeats each word. רבי זירא, who says he is silenced, speaks of someone who repeats a whole verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is where he says each word and repeats it. That case is where he says each verse and repeats it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 34 by showing that רבי זירא and the ברייתא are talking about two different kinds of repeating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating single words is ugly and spoils the reading, so the ברייתא calls it מגונה, but we do not stop him. Repeating a whole verse looks like he is accepting two separate powers, the same problem as 'מודים מודים', so רבי זירא says we silence him. Both sources are now true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer that splits a contradiction into two cases.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Repeating a word is the milder case, which is only מגונה. Repeating a whole verse is the more serious case, where he is silenced.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: repeating a full verse of שמע is treated like 'מודים מודים', and the חזן is silenced.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא, דְּאָמַר מִילְּתָא מִילְּתָא וְתָנֵי לַהּ.
phrases.english: This one is where he says each word and repeats it.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's case. It is only מגונה, and he is not silenced.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא, דְּאָמַר פְּסוּקָא פְּסוּקָא וְתָנֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: And that one is where he says each verse and repeats it.
phrases.notes: This is רבי זירא's case. He is silenced, because it looks like he accepts two powers.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא, דְּאָמַר מִילְּתָא מִילְּתָא וְתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 34
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different way of repeating
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating שמע is one single case, so רבי זירא and the ברייתא truly argue.
steps.terutzMaskana: Repeating a word is מגונה but not silenced. Repeating a verse is silenced.

steps.title: Maybe he repeated only because he lacked focus the first time
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: perhaps the person who repeated the verse did not have כוונה the first time, and he said it again to say it properly with כוונה. If so, why should he be silenced? The line ends as אביי begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But perhaps at first he did not focus his mind, and in the end he did focus his mind? He said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the rule that repeating a verse gets the person silenced. He offers an innocent reason for repeating. The last words, 'אמר ליה', set up אביי's answer, which comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silencing assumes that repeating shows a bad idea, namely accepting two powers. רב פפא points out a harmless reason instead: the person may have lacked כוונה the first time and repeated the verse to fix it. If that is possible, silencing him seems unfair.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps. This is a common opener for a challenge that offers another possibility.
He focused his mind. This means he had כוונה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But perhaps at first he did not focus his mind,
and in the end he did focus his mind?
phrases.notes: If so, the repeat was for כוונה and not for two powers. Why silence him?

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him:
phrases.notes: This only opens אביי's reply. The answer itself continues in the next section.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: וְדִילְמָא מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא כַּוֵּון דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from Step 35 that repeating a verse gets the person silenced
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that someone who repeats a full verse of שמע is silenced
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repeating could come from an innocent reason, namely fixing missing כוונה. So it does not prove a heretical idea, and silencing him seems unjustified.
